newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia approves Proton plant in India.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia approves Proton plant in India.

text.p: Malaysia's cabinet has approved investment plans by national carmaker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd's (Proton) to build a car plant in India, government officials said on Thursday.
They said Proton would set up a car manufacturing plant in the south Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, whose Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu ended a visit to Malaysia on Thursday.
"We were told that (on Wednesday) the (Malaysian) cabinet decided to clear the Proton plant. Now they can set up in Andhra Pradesh," Naidu told Reuters.
"In principle the (Malaysian) cabinet has accepted. They have asked me to send a letter from the government of India. Other procedures will follow."

He said he had asked India's Industry Minister Murasoli Maran to send the letter. The original offer to build a Proton plant in India was made to the south Indian state of Tamil Nadu, a spokesman for Malaysia's Works Minister Samy Vellu said.
"Now after the chief minister appealed to the Prime Minister (Mahathir Mohamad), the project is being shifted," he said.
"There is an agreement in principle. Malaysia will send a team to Andhra Pradesh to make a feasibility study," he said.
Naidu said he expected work to start soon on the project, which would be a full-fledged manufacturing plant, but was unsure when the plant would be begin operating or the costs involved.
"They want port facilities, so it will be (located) preferably at Vizag (Visakhapatnam) or Kakinada," Naidu said.
After Proton decided on the investment required, it would tie up with an Indian partner to set up the plant, Naidu said.

The Malaysian government has also agreed to a high-speed telecommunications link between a high-technology industrial park located in the Andhra Pradesh capital Hyderabad and Malaysia's Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC) near Kuala Lumpur.
India would also be sending skilled workers to the MSC to help develop software, he said.
The MSC is an information technology zone Malaysia is developing south of Kuala Lumpur.
Naidu said about 30 industrialists and officials on his team discussed various projects with Malaysian companies.
Diversified IJM Corporation Bhd has signed a joint venture agreement with India's Satyam Computers to set up a 300-megawatt power plant in Andhra Pradesh.

On Tuesday, Bina Puri Holdings Bhd announced it had signed a joint venture agreement with an Indian company, Madhucon Projects Ltd, to build flyovers in Hyderabad and a 75-km (47-mile) highway in the state. The projects are worth 120 million ringgit ($47.62 million).

Indian High Commission officials said contracts and projects worth 20 billion ringgit ($7.9 billion) were under discussion by the delegation with Malaysian companies for road construction, port development, education, information technology and power projects.
